{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793143038152,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fa74961001m0K0bq0JcX78iw","messageID":"msg_17fa745ba0012sQ8YR6XaiQHNR","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing the CUDA host link launcher is actually g++ from nvidia-cuda-toolkit, which works fine with plain `-fopenmp` for linking, since CMake's CUDA compiler resolves to Debian's nvcc using g++ as the host linker.\n\nI'm weighing options for making this portable: using OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX directly doesn't cleanly cover CUDA linking, and linking against gomp isn't portable across compilers like clang's libomp. I'm considering whether CMake exposes a way to detect the actual link launcher so the right flag variant gets applied automatically.\n\nSince nvcc accepts `-Xcompiler -fopenmp` at link time, I'll just make the flag conditional in CMake based on whether a host link launcher is set, falling back to that syntax otherwise. The compile step itself seemed fine already -- the failure was specifically at link time -- so I'll implement that conditional logic now.\n\n","time":{"start":1793143032161,"end":1793143038096},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793143038152,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fa76093001UlPhRcr3iBMSHb","messageID":"msg_17fa745ba0012sQ8YR6XaiQHNR","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"text","text":"The Debian toolkit sets a host `g++` as the CUDA link launcher, so `-fopenmp` must be passed directly there. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793143707640,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fb170e1001MWperUOiJf3u2I","messageID":"msg_17fb16cc0001ti1r8G0GWv3AKm","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"reasoning","text":"Hybrid doesn't seem to help at np1, likely because the 256 CPU threads interfere or run slowly on their chunks—each CPU chunk of 16 rows at N=4096 involves hundreds of megaflops, which could be creating tail latency that makes the GPU wait.\n\nThe real fix is sizing the CPU chunk so its runtime matches a GPU chunk's runtime, around 4 rows instead of 16, which cuts tail latency substantially. The GPU chunk size of 256 rows also carries its own tail cost, so shrinking that too could help balance the schedule further.\n\nI'm also second-guessing whether the CPU is actually contributing useful throughput or just adding scheduling overhead — I can't easily isolate CPU-only performance here since the GPU can't be disabled mid-run. Looking at the np4 result (169ms vs np1's 346ms), the scaling is roughly 2x rather than the expected 4x across four GPUs, which points to PCIe contention from each rank uploading its own 128MB B matrix concurrently as the likely bottleneck.\n\nBreaking down the N=4096 GPU-only timing: B upload (~10ms), A/C transfers (~25ms), leaving ~300ms for the kernel itself. That works out to roughly 457 GFLOPS, which is about 82% of the RTX 3090's 556 GFLOPS FP64 peak — a genuinely strong kernel efficiency number.\n\nIf the GPU's already near peak, the CPU hybrid should theoretically add capacity, but since observed hybrid runs are slower, something's causing contention or the CPU chunks are underperforming. I should test by tweaking CPU_CHUNK and GPU_CHUNK values directly in the source and rerun experiments to isolate the bottleneck.\n\n","time":{"start":1793143697633,"end":1793143707591},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I'll test smaller chunk sizes to check this.","time":{"start":1793143707595,"end":1793143707609}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793143746095,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fb20677001YegKYBEb0kU6LT","messageID":"msg_17fb20204001J3hsdHKgMaUurq","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"reasoning","text":"The hybrid approach is still slower than GPU-only, so I'm suspecting the CPU threads are actually hurting rather than helping — likely by starving the GPU driver thread of a core to schedule on, since with 256 OpenMP threads all competing for logical CPUs, the driver thread responsible for issuing GPU copies gets preempted.\n\nWith 256 threads for 256 logical CPUs, cudaMemcpy's default spin-wait behavior could be burning CPU cycles and contending against the driver thread for scheduling time. I should test reserving a core or switching to blocking sync, but first I want to just measure the trend by running with small thread counts like 2, 16, and 64 to see how much the CPU workers actually help versus hurt.\n\n","time":{"start":1793143735927,"end":1793143746038},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793143746096,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fb22dfa001TLd8VpK7jeXG1d","messageID":"msg_17fb20204001J3hsdHKgMaUurq","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"text","text":"Shrinking the chunks did not close the gap, so tail latency is not the main cause. I'm wondering if the collapse comes from thread contention starving the GPU driver thread when running with many parallel threads, so I want to test by measuring the GPU driver's timing directly against a CPU-only baseline.\n\nActually I think I've found it: with hundreds of CPU threads spinning at 100%, the CFS scheduler only gives the spinning CUDA driver thread its fair 1/Nth share of a core, which is far too little to service GPU calls promptly — that's the collapse. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793143864967,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fb3d4f5001wVnb3pb5GB7sl1","messageID":"msg_17fb3cb7f001vPx3W9Uoujbn3S","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"reasoning","text":"Maybe the bottleneck isn't GPU spin-waiting but the CPU worker threads themselves—with 255 threads splitting the work, the CPU side might be the slow part, finishing work in a long tail while the GPU idles after completing its chunks sooner.\n\nActually the math doesn't support that—a single 4-row chunk should finish in milliseconds of pure compute. The real issue is likely memory bandwidth: each chunk streams the entire 128MB B matrix, so 255 threads doing this per tiny 4-row block generates enormous DRAM traffic, far exceeding available bandwidth. This points to the row-blocking being too fine-grained for efficient cache reuse, meaning the CPU GEMM path needs much larger row blocks to amortize B panel reads, which conflicts with the dynamic fine-grained chunking scheme—so I'm weighing whether to drop CPU compute from the hybrid entirely and rely on GPU only, reserving OpenMP for initialization and validation instead.\n\nA static split with memory contention still seems unavoidable, and I'm concluding that hybrid CPU participation isn't actually worth it here given the B-streaming memory bound and the GPU already near its DP peak — so maximum performance really comes from GPU kernel quality plus MPI scale-out. I'll use OpenMP more narrowly, for host-side work like parallel initialization and validation, rather than forcing CPU compute into the main GEMM path.\n\nI tested this: CPU participation hurt performance at every thread count I tried (2 threads gave 387 vs 403 GPU-only, 8 threads dropped to 258), confirming the bottleneck is memory bandwidth contention with the GPU driver. So I'm dropping the CPU compute worker and scheduler entirely, keeping OpenMP limited to initialization since the hybrid approach measurably underperforms GPU-only execution.\n\n","time":{"start":1793143854325,"end":1793143864958},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

                                                   \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,          \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                        \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                             \\\n        }                                                                             \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// GPU tiling parameters\nconstexpr size_t TILE = 64;                 // C tile edge computed by one thread block\nconstexpr size_t TK = 16;                   // k-depth staged in shared memory per step\nconstexpr size_t REG = 4;                   // C elements per thread along each dimension\nconstexpr size_t THREADS_DIM = TILE / REG;  // 16 -> 256 threads per block\n\n// Row chunk streamed through the GPU per pipeline stage (rows of the rank-local block)\nconstexpr size_t GPU_CHUNK_ROWS = 128;\n\n// Tiled FP64 GEMM. Every C element is accumulated in a single register over\n// k = 0..N-1 in increasing order using FMA.\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(THREADS_DIM * THREADS_DIM)\nmatmulTiledKernel(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n                  double* __restrict__ C, const size_t rows, const size_t N) {\n    __shared__ double As[TK][TILE];  // As[k][m]: transposed A tile\n    __shared__ double Bs[TK][TILE];  // Bs[k][n]\n\n    const size_t tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t tx = tid % THREADS_DIM;\n    const size_t ty = tid / THREADS_DIM;\n    const size_t rowBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * TILE;\n    const size_t colBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * TILE;\n\n    double acc[REG][REG];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < REG; ++i) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < REG; ++j) {\n            acc[i][j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += TK) {\n        for (size_t l = tid; l < TILE * TK; l += THREADS_DIM * THREADS_DIM) {\n            const size_t m = l / TK;\n            const size_t kk = l % TK;\n            const size_t gr = rowBase + m;\n            const size_t gk = k0 + kk;\n            As[kk][m] = (gr < rows && gk < N) ? A[gr * N + gk] : 0.0;\n        }\n        for (size_t l = tid; l < TK * TILE; l += THREADS_DIM * THREADS_DIM) {\n            const size_t kk = l / TILE;\n            const size_t n = l % TILE;\n            const size_t gk = k0 + kk;\n            const size_t gc = colBase + n;\n            Bs[kk][n] = (gk < N && gc < N) ? B[gk * N + gc] : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n#pragma unroll\n        for (size_t kk = 0; kk < TK; ++kk) {\n            double a[REG];\n            double b[REG];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < REG; ++i) a[i] = As[kk][ty * REG + i];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < REG; ++j) b[j] = Bs[kk][tx * REG + j];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < REG; ++i) {\n#pragma unroll\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < REG; ++j) {\n                    acc[i][j] = fma(a[i], b[j], acc[i][j]);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < REG; ++i) {\n        const size_t gr = rowBase + ty * REG + i;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < REG; ++j) {\n            const size_t gc = colBase + tx * REG + j;\n            if (gr < rows && gc < N) {\n                C[gr * N + gc] = acc[i][j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Computes C_h = A_h * B_d for the `rows` local rows. Row chunks are pipelined over two\n// CUDA streams with double-buffered device memory, so the upload of one chunk, its kernel,\n// and the download of an earlier chunk overlap. Each stream keeps its own chunks in order.\nvoid gpuMultiply(const double* A_h, double* C_h, const double* B_d, const size_t rows,\n                 const size_t N) {\n    constexpr int NSTREAMS = 2;\n    const size_t chunkRows = std::min(GPU_CHUNK_ROWS, std::max<size_t>(rows, 1));\n\n    cudaStream_t streams[NSTREAMS];\n    double* dA[NSTREAMS];\n    double* dC[NSTREAMS];\n    for (int s = 0; s < NSTREAMS; ++s) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreate(&streams[s]));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA[s], chunkRows * N * sizeof(double)));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC[s], chunkRows * N * sizeof(double)));\n    }\n\n    size_t chunk = 0;\n    for (size_t begin = 0; begin < rows; begin += GPU_CHUNK_ROWS, ++chunk) {\n        const size_t m = std::min(GPU_CHUNK_ROWS, rows - begin);\n        const int s = static_cast<int>(chunk % NSTREAMS);\n\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(dA[s], A_h + begin * N, m * N * sizeof(double),\n                                   cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, streams[s]));\n\n        const dim3 block(static_cast<unsigned int>(THREADS_DIM * THREADS_DIM));\n        const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((N + TILE - 1) / TILE),\n                        static_cast<unsigned int>((m + TILE - 1) / TILE));\n        matmulTiledKernel<<<grid, block, 0, streams[s]>>>(dA[s], B_d, dC[s], m, N);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpyAsync(C_h + begin * N, dC[s], m * N * sizeof(double),\n                                   cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, streams[s]));\n    }\n\n    for (int s = 0; s < NSTREAMS; ++s) {\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(streams[s]));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA[s]));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC[s]));\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamDestroy(streams[s]));\n    }\n}\n\n// Fills `rowCount` rows starting at global row `rowBegin` of an N-column matrix (OpenMP)\nvoid initRows(double* mat, const size_t N, const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowCount) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t li = 0; li < rowCount; ++li) {\n        const size_t i = rowBegin + li;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[li * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Block distribution of N rows over `size` ranks\nvoid rowRange(const size_t N, const int size, const int rank, size_t& begin, size_t& count) {\n    const size_t base = N / static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t rem = N % static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    count = base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0);\n    begin = r * base + std::min(r, rem);\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const double* B, const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n\n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n\n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += getPseudoRndValue(N, i, k) * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n\n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n\n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    int status = -1;  // -1: continue running, otherwise exit code\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            const int n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n            if (n <= 0 || n > INT_MAX) {\n                if (root) printf(\"Invalid matrix size: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                status = 1;\n                break;\n            }\n            N = static_cast<size_t>(n);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            status = 0;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            status = 1;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (status >= 0) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return status;\n    }\n\n    // Bind each rank to a GPU on its node\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    const cudaError_t devErr = cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount);\n    if (devErr != cudaSuccess || deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Rank %d: no usable CUDA device (%s)\\n\", rank,\n                devErr == cudaSuccess ? \"none found\" : cudaGetErrorString(devErr));\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaSetDevice(localRank % deviceCount));\n\n    // Divide host cores among the ranks sharing this node (used for OpenMP host work)\n    const int hostThreads = std::max(1, omp_get_max_threads() / localSize);\n    omp_set_num_threads(hostThreads);\n\n    size_t rowBegin = 0;\n    size_t rowCount = 0;\n    rowRange(N, size, rank, rowBegin, rowCount);\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"Parallelization: MPI (%d ranks) + OpenMP (%d threads/rank) + CUDA (1 GPU/rank)\\n\",\n               size, hostThreads);\n    }\n\n    // Allocate matrices (pinned host memory for asynchronous transfers)\n    const size_t localElems = std::max<size_t>(rowCount, 1) * N;\n    double* A_h = nullptr;\n    double* B_h = nullptr;\n    double* C_h = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(&A_h, localElems * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(&B_h, N * N * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(&C_h, localElems * sizeof(double)));\n\n    double* dB = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, N * N * sizeof(double)));\n\n    // Initialize matrices (each rank generates its rows of A and all of B)\n    if (root) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initRows(A_h, N, rowBegin, rowCount);\n    initRows(B_h, N, 0, N);\n\n    // Perform matrix multiplication\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, B_h, N * N * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    gpuMultiply(A_h, C_h, dB, rowCount, N);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    const double localSec = std::chrono::duration<double>(end - start).count();\n    double maxSec = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localSec, &maxSec, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (root) {\n        auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n            std::chrono::duration<double>(maxSec));\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", static_cast<long>(duration.count()));\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Gather the full result on rank 0 only when it is needed for output or validation\n    const bool needFull = printResults || validate;\n    std::vector<double> C;\n    if (needFull) {\n        if (root) C.resize(N * N);\n\n        MPI_Datatype rowType;\n        MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(N), MPI_DOUBLE, &rowType);\n        MPI_Type_commit(&rowType);\n\n        std::vector<int> counts(size);\n        std::vector<int> displs(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            size_t b = 0;\n            size_t c = 0;\n            rowRange(N, size, r, b, c);\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(c);\n            displs[r] = static_cast<int>(b);\n        }\n        MPI_Gatherv(C_h, static_cast<int>(rowCount), rowType,\n                    root ? C.data() : nullptr, counts.data(), displs.data(), rowType,\n                    0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        MPI_Type_free(&rowType);\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults && root) {\n        print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    int valid = 1;\n    if (validate) {\n        if (root) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            valid = validateResult(B_h, C, N) ? 1 : 0;\n            if (valid) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            }\n        }\n        MPI_Bcast(&valid, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFreeHost(A_h));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFreeHost(B_h));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFreeHost(C_h));\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return (validate && !valid) ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/matmul/matmul.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/matmul/matmul.cpp","time":{"start":1793143946292,"end":1793143946332}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17fb4fb0f0015tp2KjCsNx0VGM","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","messageID":"msg_17fb4f046001kGMelLnjpuGtxK"}}

I need to flag that the new FMA-consistent code won't produce bit-identical hashes to the old GCC-contracted build, clarify that OpenMP's role is limited to initialization only, note behavior changes like rejecting N<=0, requiring a GPU, and new output lines, and mention that testing was limited to a single node with 4 GPUs rather than a multi-node cluster.\n\n","time":{"start":1793144220519,"end":1793144226647},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793144227702,"sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","part":{"id":"prt_17fb9835d00107XecAmhQm2sXq","messageID":"msg_17fb96717001pHbkMhEXswwJjB","sessionID":"ses_e805c2e6cffevvvxQwcZPp6MDK","type":"text","text":"The hybrid build is in place. `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` are the only files changed, and the executable is still `matmul`.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** C is split into row blocks across ranks. Each rank generates its own rows of A and all of B with the same formula, so nothing is communicated before the multiply. Rank 0 gathers C only when `-r` or `-v` needs it.\n- **CUDA:** each rank binds to a node-local GPU and runs a tiled, register-blocked FP64 kernel (64×64 tiles, 4×4 per thread). Row chunks are pipelined over two streams with double-buffered device memory, so transfers overlap the kernel. The GPU is mandatory; the program aborts if none is found.\n- **OpenMP:** used for the parallel matrix initialization. Host cores are divided among the ranks on a node.\n\n**Verification (RTX 3090 ×4, single node)**\n- The `-r` hash matches a reference computed with fused multiply-add for N = 1, 7, 100, 511, 1000 at 1–4 ranks. The scratch program that computes this reference lives outside the repo.\n- `-v` passes for odd, small, and non-tile-multiple sizes, including ranks with zero rows.\n\n| N | 1 rank | 2 ranks | 4 ranks | Original (serial) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1024 | 307 GFLOP/s | 537 | 307 | 0.27 |\n| 2048 | 373 | 716 | 687 | — |\n| 4096 | 505 | 904 | 1580 | — |\n\nThe 4-rank N=1024 run was slower than 2 ranks, and the sample is small, so I did not investigate it further.\n\n**Things you should know**\n- **Output hashes change.** The original is not bit-stable: GCC fuses some multiply-adds and not others, and one element matches neither form. The new code uses FMA consistently, so `-r` hashes will differ from the original binary in the last bits. Validation still passes.\n- **CPU co-computation was tried and removed.** OpenMP threads taking row chunks alongside the GPU reduced throughput at every thread count I measured. The CPU path is DRAM-bound, and the GPU kernel already reaches about 80% of the card's FP64 peak. Because of this, OpenMP's role is limited to initialization.\n- **Behavior changes:** `-n 0` and negative sizes are rejected. Output gained a \"Parallelization:\" line and a launch hint in the usage text. Timing is the maximum across ranks and includes host-device transfers.\n- **Build:** the CUDA link flags handle both the Debian toolkit (host `g++` launcher) and stock CMake (`nvcc` launcher).\n- **Not tested:** multiple nodes. The MPI scaling numbers come from one node only.","time":{"start":1793144226653,"end":1793144227698}}}
